title: Shiva the hunter
hookLine: a boar charges, two arrows strike it at once, and Arjuna sneers at a mountain hunter who is Shiva
carry: the divine can come as the one you dismiss
tomorrow: how will Arjuna see who the hunter is?

lines: A BOAR CRASHES THROUGH THE TREES.
cards: Crashing through the trees, a boar. It's huge, and it's coming straight at Arjuna. The story tells us it's no ordinary animal: a demon named Muka has taken this shape to kill the man at prayer.
Thin from fasting, Arjuna still moves fast. He grabs his bow, nocks an arrow and draws.
And at that very moment, someone else is drawing too: a hunter, a Kirata, one of the mountain people, with a woman at his side and a crowd behind him. Two archers. One boar.

teach.h: THE HUNTER IS SHIVA IN DISGUISE.
teach.b: The listener knows something Arjuna doesn't. The hunter is Shiva, come down the mountain in disguise, and the woman beside him is his consort Uma, also disguised. Stop, the hunter calls.
I aimed at that boar first.
Arjuna ignores him and shoots. So does the hunter. Both arrows strike at the same instant, and the boar falls dead, in its own demon shape again.
Arjuna is furious. Who are you, he demands? Why did you shoot the game I had already marked?
That breaks the rules of the hunt. I'll take your life for it. The hunter isn't impressed.
This forest is our home, he says. I claimed that boar first. Look at the turn.
After all that discipline, the first stranger Arjuna meets makes him furious in seconds, and he speaks to him like a nobody from the hills. And the nobody is Shiva.
This is one of the deep patterns of Hindu storytelling: God comes in disguise, as a hunter, a beggar, a guest at the door.

teach.h: GOD IN THE ONE YOU DISMISS.
teach.b: Shiva as the Kirata, the hunter, is honored as one of his forms, and Hindu belief holds that the divine can take any form it chooses.
An old Upanishad puts it in three words many Hindu children learn: atithi devo bhava, let the guest be God to you. That's part of why so many Hindus meet a stranger with folded hands.
Arjuna's austerities have made him strong. They haven't yet made him see. And he's about to pick a fight with the very god he came to find.

how: The meeting of Arjuna and Shiva as a hunter is retold in Hindu storytelling, poetry and temple art, and Shiva in the guise of a Kirata is honored as a form of the god; stories of the divine arriving in disguise run all through Hindu tradition.

o: a hunter's rule about who may claim the game
the disguise Shiva wears on the mountain
Arjuna's discipline: strong now, but not yet humble

games.q: the boar and the hunter — tap the pairs.
p: a demon in the shape of a boar
let the guest be God to you

s: he took him for a mountain hunter and threatened him.
Shiva as the Kirata, the hunter, is honored as one of his forms
the hunter Arjuna dismissed is worshipped as a form of the god.
the boar was an ordinary animal
it was a demon named Muka who had taken that shape to kill Arjuna.

games.q: you're Arjuna. a rough stranger from the hills has shot the boar with you. knowing how Hindu stories go, what's the wiser move?
o: ask who he is before you threaten him.
threaten him; a hunter can't match a prince.
walk away; he isn't worth your time.
games.why: Arjuna threatened him instead. the hunter was Shiva: in Hindu stories, God often comes as the one you'd least expect.

practice: Bring to mind someone you brushed off lately: a stranger, a coworker, a kid, someone at the door. See their face as you breathe in. As you breathe out, fold your hands, the old Hindu greeting, namaste: I bow to you.
If you pray, ask to see the holy in that person; if not, just wish them well.

wordCard.voice: Arjuna's austerities. They've made him strong enough to face a demon boar, and quick enough to sneer at a hunter who is Shiva.

orig.note: Sanskrit kirāta: a mountain hunter; Shiva's disguise in this story.

carryVoice: Your line: the divine can come as the one you dismiss. Arjuna didn't see it was Shiva. Tomorrow: how will Arjuna see who the hunter is?

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), Kairata Parva (Shiva comes as a Kirata with Uma; the danava Muka as a boar; Arjuna and the Kirata shoot together; the quarrel)
Taittiriya Upanishad 1.11.2 (atithi devo bhava: let the guest be as God to you)
